- [ ] `utterances` + `attestations` replace `statements`; `said_at_precision`; `clusters`, `stances`, `findings`.

- `1.7` One thing said, reported by several documents, is one utterance with several attestations.
  <details><summary>Detail</summary>

  A speech carried by five outlets is one thing that was said and five documents reporting
  it. Stored as five records instead, a persona's timeline is five copies of one sentence,
  and analysis compares them with each other and reads the echo as agreement. Identity is
  the speaker, the date, and the folded text; the utterance keeps the fullest wording any
  document carries, because a quote trimmed for space should not become the record.
  </details>

- `1.8` An utterance records the venue it was made in and the audience it was addressed to; an attestation records who reported it.
  <details><summary>Detail</summary>

  Two different things, and both are needed. *Where it was said and to whom* is a property
  of the speech act — the same words to a committee and to a rally are two utterances, and
  the difference between them is the point of an anomaly. *Who reported it* is a property
  of each document. For an op-ed the two coincide, which is consistent rather than
  contradictory: the venue is that publication and there is one attestation from it.
  </details>

- `1.9` A date a source establishes only to the month is stored as a month — distinct from a day and from unknown.
  <details><summary>Detail</summary>

  Thirty years back, a source often gives "March 1998" and no more. Recording that as the
  first of the month invents a fact a timeline will then sort by; recording it as unknown
  throws away most of what the source did say. Three states, carried separately: a date
  with the precision it was established to, and no date at all.
  </details>

--
-- Nothing is ever overwritten: a re-run under a new model or prompt writes its own row
-- beside the old one, and the pair is what tells them apart.
CREATE TABLE stances (
  id             TEXT PRIMARY KEY,      -- ULID, minted once
  utterance_id   TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES utterances(id),
  cluster_id     TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES clusters(id),
  position       REAL NOT NULL,         -- -1..1 along the cluster's axis
  confidence     REAL NOT NULL,         -- 0..1
  model_version  TEXT NOT NULL,
  prompt_version TEXT NOT NULL,
  created_at     TEXT NOT NULL,
  UNIQUE (utterance_id, model_version, prompt_version)
);

CREATE INDEX stances_by_cluster ON stances (cluster_id, utterance_id);

-- A surfaced inconsistency. The two kinds answer different questions, and the table
-- refuses a record that is missing its own answer: an anomaly's point is who they were
-- talking to, a trend change's is when it moved. Stored without those, a finding reads
-- as complete and is not.
CREATE TABLE findings (
  id             TEXT PRIMARY KEY,      -- ULID, minted once
  figure_id      TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES figures(id),
  cluster_id     TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES clusters(id),
  kind           TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (kind IN ('anomaly', 'trend-change')),
  rationale      TEXT NOT NULL,
  score          REAL NOT NULL,
  -- An anomaly's point. Audience stays nullable: plenty of sources establish the venue
  -- and say nothing about who was in the room.
  venue          TEXT,
  audience       TEXT,
  -- A trend change's point, as an interval. A series bounds the change between two
  -- observations and no further, so a single date would be a claim it cannot make.
  changed_after  TEXT,
  changed_before TEXT,
  model_version  TEXT NOT NULL,
  prompt_version TEXT NOT NULL,
  created_at     TEXT NOT NULL,
  superseded_by  TEXT REFERENCES findings(id),
  surfaced       INTEGER NOT NULL,
  CHECK (
    (kind = 'anomaly'      AND venue IS NOT NULL AND changed_after IS NULL     AND changed_before IS NULL)
    OR
    (kind = 'trend-change' AND venue IS NULL     AND audience IS NULL
                           AND changed_after IS NOT NULL AND changed_before IS NOT NULL)
  )
);

CREATE INDEX findings_live ON findings (figure_id, cluster_id, superseded_by);

-- Which utterances a finding rests on, and what each one is doing in it: the deviating
-- one for an anomaly, the two either side of the change point for a trend change.
CREATE TABLE finding_utterances (
  finding_id   TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES findings(id),
  utterance_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES utterances(id),
  role         TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (role IN ('deviating', 'before', 'after')),
  PRIMARY KEY (finding_id, utterance_id)
);

The rest of #34 phase 3's data model, additive beside everything v1 shipped.

missing the attribute its kind turns on — an anomaly without the venue it was
addressed to, a trend change without the interval the change falls in. Stored
without those, a finding reads as complete and is not.

input.body:
The second half of #34's phase 3. The first half — `utterances` and `attestations` — landed in #40; the analysis records the stance series is read off did not.

## What this needs

- `clusters` and the assignment of an utterance to one, so a subject can be opened by an utterance rather than chosen from a committed vocabulary. The label is regenerated from the members and is display only.
- `stances` — one utterance's position on one cluster's axis, with the model and prompt version that produced it. Embedding distance measures aboutness, not agreement, so position has to be a recorded judgment.
- `findings` — the two kinds the stance series produces, each carrying the utterances it rests on, superseded rather than overwritten.

## Exit

The phase-3 exit condition #34 states that #40 could not reach: **supersede-not-overwrite holds for findings.** Plus, from the design: a finding cannot be stored missing the attribute its kind turns on — an anomaly's venue and audience, a trend change's interval.

Purely additive, so it is an expand step under #37's discipline and needs no reader migration.

Refs #34, #40

**What changed and why.** v1 (#25) shipped a corpus of flat statements judged in pairs against a topic list read off the source. Three things break that at the scale now intended — decades of archives, many sources, a big roster: one speech carried by five outlets became five statements; pairwise judging is O(n²) and cannot see a trend at all; and a topic vocabulary decides in advance what the corpus may be about. The replacement is utterances with many attestations, subjects discovered by embedding, and a stance series per persona per subject.

**This is cheap now and expensive later.** The corpus is fixtures, so this is a rewrite of code and spec, not a migration of cited data. After the first real source it becomes the hard case the stable-id promise exists to prevent.

## Phases

**0. Provisioning (human-only, front-loaded)** — see the comment added to #27
- [ ] Vectorize index created and bound; Workflows enabled on the account.
- [ ] The embedding model and the stance model chosen, both reachable from the Worker.
- [ ] Exit: `wrangler deploy --dry-run` resolves the new bindings from the committed config.

**1. Verify the Workflow bet**
- [ ] Read Cloudflare's published step, duration and payload limits for Workflows and check a one-year archive slice against them. **They could not be read from the session that wrote the design** — the doc says so rather than asserting numbers.
- [ ] Exit: either a slice size that provably fits, or a recorded decision to slice smaller / move the stage.

**2. Spec first**
- [ ] Rewrite the affected leaves in `dev/requirements/requirements.md`: utterance vs attestation, date precision, roster resolution (#31), emergent clusters, stance, the two finding kinds. Watch the coverage gate go red before any case exists.
- [ ] Exit: the gate is red for exactly the new leaves, green once claimed.

**3. Data model**
- [ ] `utterances` + `attestations` replace `statements`; `said_at_precision`; `clusters`, `stances`, `findings`.
- [ ] Exit: logic cases prove one speech across three documents is one utterance and three attestations; that a month-precision date is neither a day nor unknown; that supersede-not-overwrite still holds for findings.

**4. Ingestion**
- [ ] The pipeline as one module — fetch, extract, resolve, merge, embed, assign, stance — every stage idempotent under retry.
- [ ] Exit: behavior cases prove a replayed payload writes nothing new, an unrostered speaker is retained unattributed, and the same quote at three lengths merges to one utterance.

**5. Embedding, clustering, stance**
- [ ] Vector store and stance model behind interfaces a case can script; online cluster assignment; stance stored with model and prompt version.
- [ ] Exit: cases over fixtures where the *source* topic strings deliberately disagree still cluster together (#33), and a scripted stance model produces a readable series.

**6. Detection**
- [ ] Anomaly (deviation from prevailing stance, carrying venue and audience) and trend change (change point, reported as an interval).
- [ ] Exit: cases over a synthetic series with a planted step change and a planted outlier find each, and find nothing in a flat series.

**7. Backfill Workflow**
- [ ] One run per archive slice, sharing the ingestion code, resumable per step.
- [ ] Exit: a slice runs end to end against fixtures; a deliberately failed step retries without re-fetching.

**8. API and site**
- [ ] `/api/v1` and the six pages carry utterances, attestations and findings. The inconsistency page keeps its shape: the two representative utterances either side of a change point.
- [ ] Exit: server and screen lanes green; goldens refreshed and reviewed.

Ordering: 0 and 1 front-loaded → 2 → 3 → 4 → {5, 6} → 7 → 8. Review lands as one stack, not a wait per phase.

## Out of scope

*Why* a trend changed — the design settles for when. Cross-persona comparison. Anything that would need a source we have not agreed to take.

The design doc carries the end state and the rationale; this issue carries only the phases and their exit conditions. Append-only once agreed.

**What changed and why.** v1 (#25) shipped a corpus of flat statements judged in pairs against a topic list read off the source. Three things break that at the scale now intended — decades of archives, many sources, a big roster: one speech carried by five outlets became five statements; pairwise judging is O(n²) and cannot see a trend at all; and a topic vocabulary decides in advance what the corpus may be about. The replacement is utterances with many attestations, subjects discovered by embedding, and a stance series per persona per subject.

**This is cheap now and expensive later.** The corpus is fixtures, so this is a rewrite of code and spec, not a migration of cited data. After the first real source it becomes the hard case the stable-id promise exists to prevent.

## Phases

**0. Provisioning (human-only, front-loaded)** — see the comment added to #27
- [ ] Vectorize index created and bound; Workflows enabled on the account.
- [ ] The embedding model and the stance model chosen, both reachable from the Worker.
- [ ] Exit: `wrangler deploy --dry-run` resolves the new bindings from the committed config.

**1. Verify the Workflow bet**
- [ ] Read Cloudflare's published step, duration and payload limits for Workflows and check a one-year archive slice against them. **They could not be read from the session that wrote the design** — the doc says so rather than asserting numbers.
- [ ] Exit: either a slice size that provably fits, or a recorded decision to slice smaller / move the stage.

**2. Spec first**
- [ ] Rewrite the affected leaves in `dev/requirements/requirements.md`: utterance vs attestation, date precision, roster resolution (#31), emergent clusters, stance, the two finding kinds. Watch the coverage gate go red before any case exists.
- [ ] Exit: the gate is red for exactly the new leaves, green once claimed.

**3. Data model**
- [ ] `utterances` + `attestations` replace `statements`; `said_at_precision`; `clusters`, `stances`, `findings`.
- [ ] Exit: logic cases prove one speech across three documents is one utterance and three attestations; that a month-precision date is neither a day nor unknown; that supersede-not-overwrite still holds for findings.

**4. Ingestion**
- [ ] The pipeline as one module — fetch, extract, resolve, merge, embed, assign, stance — every stage idempotent under retry.
- [ ] Exit: behavior cases prove a replayed payload writes nothing new, an unrostered speaker is retained unattributed, and the same quote at three lengths merges to one utterance.

**5. Embedding, clustering, stance**
- [ ] Vector store and stance model behind interfaces a case can script; online cluster assignment; stance stored with model and prompt version.
- [ ] Exit: cases over fixtures where the *source* topic strings deliberately disagree still cluster together (#33), and a scripted stance model produces a readable series.

**6. Detection**
- [ ] Anomaly (deviation from prevailing stance, carrying venue and audience) and trend change (change point, reported as an interval).
- [ ] Exit: cases over a synthetic series with a planted step change and a planted outlier find each, and find nothing in a flat series.

**7. Backfill Workflow**
- [ ] One run per archive slice, sharing the ingestion code, resumable per step.
- [ ] Exit: a slice runs end to end against fixtures; a deliberately failed step retries without re-fetching.

**8. API and site**
- [ ] `/api/v1` and the six pages carry utterances, attestations and findings. The inconsistency page keeps its shape: the two representative utterances either side of a change point.
- [ ] Exit: server and screen lanes green; goldens refreshed and reviewed.

Ordering: 0 and 1 front-loaded → 2 → 3 → 4 → {5, 6} → 7 → 8. Review lands as one stack, not a wait per phase.

## Out of scope

*Why* a trend changed — the design settles for when. Cross-persona comparison. Anything that would need a source we have not agreed to take.

input.body:
The rest of #34's phase 3. #40 landed `utterances` and `attestations`; this lands the records the stance series is read off. Additive throughout, so `0003` is an expand step under the gate #41 just added — nothing the running Worker reads changes. ## The three records **A cluster is a row an utterance can open.** `assignToCluster(utteranceId, null)` mints one. That is the whole operational content of "subjects are discovered, not declared": the corpus becomes able to be about something new with nothing edited anywhere. The label is regenerated from the members and is display only — the case proves relabelling moves nothing by comparing the membership either side of a rename. **A stance is a recorded judgment, not geometry.** The two sentences the case uses — > «לא אצביע בעד תקציב שגורע ולו שקל אחד מהרכבת הקלה» > «הרכבת הקלה מעולם לא הייתה בעדיפות שלי» — sit close together in embedding space precisely because they are *about* the same thing, which is why distance can't tell you they conflict. So position is stored with the model and prompt that produced it. A replay under the same pair is idempotent; a re-judgment under a new prompt writes its own row beside the old one, and `stanceSeries` is always read at one model and prompt so a series can never mix two. **A finding refuses to be incomplete.** Supersede-not-overwrite (#34's stated phase-3 exit that #40 couldn't reach), plus a table-level CHECK: an anomaly must carry the venue it was addressed to, a trend change must carry the interval the change falls in, and neither can carry the other's. A record that could be stored missing its own point would read as complete and not be. ## Seeing it fail Doc-first: the four leaves went into `requirements.md` first and the coverage gate went red for exactly `1.10`–`1.13` before any case existed. For `1.13` specifically the rejection assertions are only worth anything if the CHECK is what rejects — so I removed the CHECK from `0003`, watched `1.13` go red, and put it back. ## Folders touched
**`src/backend/corpus/`** — `0003` adds `clusters`, `cluster_members`, `stances`, `findings`, `finding_utterances`. `store.ts` gains the cluster/stance/finding surface: `assignToCluster`, `relabelCluster`, `clusterOf`/`clusterMembers`, `recordStance`, `stancesFor`, `stanceSeries`, `recordFinding`, `getFinding`, `findingsFor`. **`src/shared/`** — `Cluster`, `ClusterMember`, `Stance`, `Finding` and its `FindingKind`/`FindingRole`/`ChangeWindow`. `changed` is one nullable object rather than two nullable fields, so half an interval isn't expressible in the shape a reader gets. **`dev/requirements/`** — leaves `1.10`–`1.13` with their detail blocks, four logic cases claiming them, and a `withUtterance` fixture helper for cases about what sits *above* utterances. **`docs/architecture/`** — corrects the anomaly paragraph, which still said the *attestation* carries venue and audience. They belong to the utterance, as the data-model section already said; I missed this one in #40.
## What this deliberately does not do Clustering and stance *logic* are phase 5, detection is phase 6. Nothing here decides what is near what or where a change point is — the cases script those, because a data-model case that also asserted the algorithm would be proving two things and pinning neither. ## Verification `npm run typecheck`, `npm test` (55), `npm run test:server` (11, real workerd), `npm run test:screen` (9) — green locally. `check_the_world.mjs`: 0 blocking. CI still cannot run — every workflow fails at startup, see #39. Closes #42 Refs #34 --- _Generated by [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code)_
